summary: State check (NCRB heat/sun-stroke deaths 2017-2022, 213 state-years): Poisson rate ratio per +10 'Danger' heat-index days = 1.013 (95% CI 1.008-1.018), but the data are strongly overdispersed (Pearson dispersion 37.53); the Negative Binomial model gives 1.058 (1.011-1.108). Sanity check: the paper attributes ~48 deaths/yr to heatwaves in Mumbai (3.69 per million), ~4.3x the per-capita rate of certified heat/sun-stroke deaths in Maharashtra (0.85 per million). That gap is expected (all-cause excess vs certified heatstroke, plus undercounting), so Layer 2 does not contradict Layer 1; it confirms that hotter state-years report more heat deaths.

data.outcome_source: NCRB ADSI heat/sun-stroke deaths via Parliament answers (PIB 2023 annexure; PIB Release 2158403, 20 Aug 2025)
data.exposure_source: ERA5 hourly T + RH at each state/UT capital (Open-Meteo archive, models=era5), NOAA heat index
data.population_source: Census 2011 (Wikipedia 'List of states and union territories of India by population', 2011 Census column)

poisson_danger_year.formula: deaths ~ danger_days + C(year)  (offset = log Census-2011 population)

poisson_caution_year.formula: deaths ~ extreme_caution_days + C(year)  (offset = log Census-2011 population)

negbin_danger_year.formula: deaths ~ danger_days + C(year)  (offset = log population), NB2

layer1_sanity_check.note: Not like-for-like: the paper counts ALL-CAUSE excess deaths during heatwaves (incl. heart and lung deaths, 2009-2015); NCRB counts deaths certified as heat/sun-stroke (2017-2022). Populations are from different years (MCGM 2023 estimate vs Census 2011).

caveats: Official heat deaths are known undercounts; reporting completeness differs between states.
One capital per state is a crude exposure measure for a whole state.
Population is fixed at Census 2011 (no newer official census); year effects absorb national trends.
Small sample (~200 rows): use as a sanity check, not as a predictor.
